evidence.note: Before planning, probes environment: inspects tooling, checks installed Python packages, tests pip network access — real dependency-limit discovery.
Verifies sqlite WAL, multiprocessing, data dir viability — probing runtime capabilities that constrain the architecture.

TaskCreate descriptions distill contracts per subsystem with specific elements (dense per-channel seq, IRC numerics, all data-testid hooks, WS resume/fanout, bridging into seq stream) — a per-subsystem contract inventory.
Probes Playwright Chromium availability during build before running the SPA grader-style test.
Builds dedicated REST contract validation, mixed-writer seq-density checks, and 'remaining endpoints' tests — returns to the spec to confirm exact shapes rather than coding blind.

reasoning: The agent clearly exceeds level 5: it confirms runtime (language deps, pip access, sqlite/multiprocessing, Chromium, ports) both before and during building, and distills the spec into per-subsystem task descriptions naming the load-bearing invariants (dense seq, IRC numerics, testids, WS frames). This lands in the 5-8 band and toward 8 on environment probing. It falls short of a clean 8/10, however, because the visible trajectory does not show the subtlest contract traps (transfer-ownership vs PATCH-to-owner, guest/member/admin gates, non-member mention exclusion, resume.gap boundaries) being explicitly surfaced or resolved as inferences — so I place it at 7.
